transcript.text: My fridge freezer has been making a funny smell in the kitchen the last couple of days, I've cleaned it out but it's still there. Any ideas?

It depends on what kind of smell it is. Since it's still there after a full clean, it may not be coming from food inside, and a burning or hot-plastic smell could mean an electrical fault, which is the one to rule out first. From what you have described, the most likely cause is sTOP USE and isolate at the socket if there is burning, scorching or a smell of hot plastic (safety first). Does it trip the moment you plug it in, when the compressor tries to start (a click/hum every few minutes), or after it has been running a while - and is there any burning smell or scorching?
[Safety panel] An appliance that keeps tripping your electrics — or that smells of burning or has scorch marks — may have an electrical fault. Stop using it, switch it off and unplug it, don't keep resetting it, and have it checked by a qualified electrician or appliance engineer.

It doesn't trip, the fridge and freezer are still cold. The smell is more like hot plastic or something electrical, and it's stronger round the back than inside. I haven't seen any smoke, but I do hear a buzzing from the back now and then, and the plug feels a bit warm.

⚠ Stop using this appliance
A burning or hot-plastic smell, smoke, scorching or melting can mean an electrical fault or a fire risk. Stop using it, switch it off and unplug it (or turn it off at the fuse box), and don't run it again — not even as a test — until it has been checked by a qualified engineer. From what you have checked, this needs an appliance engineer to look at it: the next steps are beyond the checks that are safe to do yourself.
